API REST pública do Inbox Autônomo Koban:
Public REST API for the Kobana Autonomous Inbox.

Authentication: Bearer JWT (RS256, issued by the Kobana authorization server; `aud` includes `https://api.inbox[.<env>].kobana.com.br`) plus mTLS terminated at CloudFront (passed through as the `cloudfront-viewer-mtls-client-cert-fingerprint` header). The JWT `org` claim (the Kobana account) resolves the caller organization; `sub` is the person and is carried for attribution only. Pick a workspace inside the organization with `X-Workspace-Id` when it has more than one.

Resource `{id}` endpoints (workspaces, inboxes, agents, webhooks) accept either the internal UUID or the resource `external_id`. POST endpoints that own an `external_id` accept it as an optional field and default it to the generated internal `id` when omitted. The `deleted_at` field is never returned in responses or in webhook payloads; soft-deleted records are filtered out instead.

All keys in responses and webhook payloads are `snake_case`. Webhook deliveries share the API serializer: the envelope carries `event` (`slug`, `id`), `delivered_at` and `workspace`; `data` nests resource snapshots (`organization`, `agent`, `inbox`, `email`, `agent_run`) plus the event-specific keys.

Without `inbox_id` the inbox is resolved from the `To:` header among the caller workspace inboxes. JWT RS256 emitido pelo Authorization Ser: RS256 JWT issued by the Kobana authorization server (`iss` = `https://account[.<env>].kobana.com.br`), verified against the public keys it publishes — this API holds no signing key and cannot mint a token. Claims: `iss`, `aud=https://api.inbox[.<env>].kobana.com.br` (may be a list; the rule is *contains*), `sub`, `jti`, `exp` (required), `scope` (space-separated list), and optional `src` (`user`|`system`). Scopes have two axes: a resource, always prefixed by the app (`inbox/emails`), and an access level — `read`, `write`, `delete`, `import`, `export` or `all`. Each request needs one verb, set by its method: `GET` reads (the resource alone), `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH` write (`inbox/emails write`), `DELETE` deletes (`inbox/emails delete`). No verb stands in for another — `write` does not delete — and `all` grants every verb. `inbox/all` is the resource catch-all — it reaches every resource and grants no verb. The granular form `inbox/emails:write` (or `:delete`) satisfies both axes for that resource on its own. A token with no `inbox/…` scope is held to its access level alone. No endpoint imports or exports in bulk, so `import`/`export` gate nothing yet. `GET /v1/me` answers any valid token.
Lista de anexos permitidos. Um anexo é p: Allow list of attachments. An attachment is processed when it matches at least one rule; inside a rule every condition given must match. `null` or `[]` processes every attachment. An attachment outside the list is ignored, never a reason to reject the e-mail: the agent does not see it, the attachment limits do not count it, and a workflow step cannot reference it.
